$comment: An INDUCED modifier-order typology. Data only, no code. Staged here for transfer to eoPriors; nothing in induction/ or modifier-order/ may hardcode any of it.

provenance.source: Induced by eoreader6 induction/stacks.js, run via scripts/induction-stacks-live-priors.mjs against Alice's Adventures in Wonderland (Project Gutenberg #11, public domain), fetched from live_priors (clovenbradshaw-ctrl/live_priors, 01-literature-books/gutenberg/pg11_Alice_s_Adventures_in_Wonderland.txt). Baked once, offline; see induction/typology.js and induction/stacks.js headers for why this never runs per-reading.
provenance.built_by: measurement, not a cited linguistic authority. The giver named on `giver` below IS the measurement itself, per II.2 of eo-constitution's CONSTITUTION.md.

notes: Every ranked token here cleared a p<0.05 binomial significance test on its own pairwise position consistency inside genuinely bound modifier stacks -- see induction/stacks.js's header for the full mechanism and why it replaced an earlier, weaker clustering-based attempt.

COVERAGE IS NARROW BY DESIGN, NOT AN OVERSIGHT: only 8 tokens cleared this evidence floor against one ~27K-token book. Lower minPairOccurrences settings recover more tokens at the cost of mixing in more contamination (pronouns, contractions) -- see scripts/induction-stacks-live-priors.mjs's own header for the measured tradeoff curve. This prior is directly useful mainly when reading Alice's Adventures in Wonderland itself, or text quoting it -- a real, disclosed limitation, not a general-purpose adjective-order table. A broader prior needs induction run across many more books from live_priors, aggregated, which has not been done yet.

NOT ALL RANKED PAIRS ARE ADJECTIVE-NOUN STRUCTURE: 6 of 8 tokens (turtle/mock, rabbit/white, hare/march) are genuine, textbook-correct head-modifier recoveries -- three of the book's most-repeated named characters (Mock Turtle, White Rabbit, March Hare), each an epithet bound tightly to its head noun every time it appears (p as low as 1.4e-17). The remaining pair (not/did) is real monotonic structure too, but verb-phrase negation ('did not'), not modifier-noun order -- disclosed here rather than filtered out, since filtering it would require semantic knowledge this mechanism does not have and should not fabricate.
This file's classOf treats each token as its own class (no clustering into named 'kinds' -- see induction/stacks.js's header for why that step was skipped for the purpose of getting usable ranks).
direction is 'pre' because this corpus's own bound stacks measured that way; a different corpus could measure 'post' and would need its own file, never this one reused with the direction flipped.
giver: induced from population "live_priors:pg11_Alice_s_Adventures_in_Wonderland.txt": 4 token pair(s) with a significant (p<0.05) monotonic position within a shared bound stack, over 8 ranked token(s); rank = a Copeland-style score built only from pairs whose relative order cleared significance
